The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a102efd4a3009423), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. statement: Let D < Z ≤ Y be labelled vertices, and suppose that Z is saturated relative to Y : (Z ∩ NY )/FY = PIY Z . Let KZ be the automorphism group induced by a factor stabilizer in Z on a reference coordinate of SY . There are KZ-normal subgroups QZ ≤ RZ ≤ PZ such that (FZ ∩ NY )/FY = QIY Z , (2.8) (NZ ∩ NY )/FY = RIY Z , (2.9) RZ/QZ ∼ = TaZ Z , mZ = aZmY . (2.10) Here aZ is a positive integer. The section RZ/QZ is a chief factor for the action of KZ on PZ: there is no KZ-normal subgroup strictly between QZ and RZ. Its factors give a Z-equivariant surjection τZY : IZ −→ IY (2.11) whose fibers have size aZ. The stabilizers in D and Z of a coordinate in IY induce the same transitive action on its fiber. In addition, suppose X < Z and the hypotheses of Proposition 2.8 hold for X < Y . Set H∗ = ρ(Xi), KZ = H∗PZ, CZ = coreKZ (H∗). Then the subgroups in (2.8) satisfy QZ = CZ ∩ PZ, KZ = H∗RZ. (2.12) Thus RZCZ/CZ ∼ = RZ/QZ is a transitive minimal normal subgroup in the coset action of KZ/CZ on H∗/CZ. The groups H∗ and KZ induce the same action on its simple factors. No assertion that this is the entire projected socle is required. If aZ = 1, the quotient PZ/RZ is soluble.
